column2: Hearing of a brahmana endowed with qualities and approved by the good, one should bring him from afar for the rite and honour him in every way.
[Bhishma said:] One should perform the rite for the gods in the forenoon and the rite for the ancestors in the afternoon, endowed with auspicious conduct, purified and diligent.
At midday one should give to men as is fitting; a gift made out of time they know to be the share of rakshasas.
What has been stepped over or licked, what was done after a quarrel, what was seen by menstruating women: they know that to be the share of rakshasas.
What has been eaten while shouted at, or by one without vows, Bharata, or touched by a dog: they know that to be the share of rakshasas.
What has hair, or has been bought or has fallen, what has been sneezed on, looked at by dogs, wept on or shaken: they know that to be the share of rakshasas.
What is eaten without Om, or with a weapon, Bharata, or by an evil-minded man: they know that to be the share of rakshasas.
What is eaten after others' leavings, or what has been shared out, in rites for gods and ancestors constantly: they know that to be the share of rakshasas.
What is blamed or reproached, or served with anger, whether in the rite for gods or for ancestors: they know that to be the share of rakshasas.
Whatever is served without an offering of ghee, and what is eaten by those of bad conduct: they know that to be the share of rakshasas.
The shares of rakshasas have been told, bull of the Bharatas. Next, hear the examination of a brahmana for the offering.
As many brahmanas as are fallen, dull or mad are not fit for the invitation, either in the rite for gods or for ancestors, king.
One with white leprosy, a leper, an impotent man, one afflicted with consumption, an epileptic, and one blind, king, are not fit for honour.
Physicians, temple priests, those who keep vows in vain, and sellers of Soma are not fit for invitation at a funeral rite.
Singers and dancers, tumblers and musicians, story-tellers and fighters, king, are not fit for invitation.
Priests of shudras, teachers of shudras, and pupils of shudras, king, are not fit for invitation.
The brahmin who questions and the one questioned, Bharata, are not fit for the funeral rite either, since they sell Brahman.
One who is made leader first in taking a lower class, a brahmana though knowing all sciences, king, is not fit for invitation.
Brahmins without fires, those who carry out the dead, thieves and fallen men, king, are not fit for invitation.
Those of unknown origin, those with a following, and the sons of appointed daughters, Bharata, are not fit for invitation at the funeral rite.
A debtor, king, a brahmana who lives on usury, one who lives by selling living beings, king, are not fit for invitation.
Those who were previously with women, those with arrow-backs, as many as there are, bull of the Bharatas, and brahmins who do not mutter, are not fit for the funeral rite.
Brahmanas have been indicated for the rite for gods and the funeral rite, bull of the Bharatas; hear again the favour to the giver and the receiver.
Even farmers who have completed their vows, rich in qualities, who know the Savitri and are active, king, are fit for invitation.
One may invite even a twice-born of good family who follows kshatriya dharma in battle, but one should never appoint a merchant at funeral rites, dear one.
A brahmana who keeps the fire, who lives in a village, who is no thief and who knows guests, king, is fit for invitation.
He who mutters the Savitri three times a day, bull of the Bharatas, who lives by alms and is active, king, is fit for invitation.
One who has set out and returned at sunrise and sunset, harmless and of slight fault, king, is fit for invitation.
A brahmana free of sin and without argument, bull of the Bharatas, wise and living by alms, king, is fit for invitation.
Even one without vows, a gambler, a thief, a seller of living beings, or a merchant, if afterward he drinks Soma, king, is fit for invitation.
Having first earned wealth by hard farming, if afterward he is host to all, he is fit for invitation, king.
What is declared the sale of Brahman, wealth earned by a woman, and what is gained by impotence, is not to be given to ancestors and gods.
A twice-born, bull of the Bharatas, who, when the conclusion is being made, does not say what is fitting, incurs the unrighteousness of a false statement about cows.
The time of a funeral rite, Yudhishthira, is for a brahmana; curds and ghee served, the waning of Soma, and forest meat.
At the conclusion of a funeral rite the brahmana should say "Svadha"; to a kshatriya one should say "May the ancestors be pleased."
At the conclusion of a funeral rite for a vaishya, Bharata, one should say "Akshayya"; for a shudra, "Svasti."
The "auspicious day" blessing in the rite for the gods is for a brahmana; for a kshatriya the same without Om is laid down; for a vaishya one should say "May the deities be pleased."

Hear the order of the rites, done by rule before: the birth ceremony and the rest in the three classes, Bharata; for brahmin and kshatriya they are spoken with mantras, and also for the vaishya, Yudhishthira.
For a brahmin the girdle is of munja grass, for a kshatriya of bowstring fibre, for a vaishya of valvaja grass: this is the rule, Yudhishthira.
Hear this dharma and adharma of the giver and the receiver: for a brahmana a falsehood is said to be a fall-making sin; fourfold for a kshatriya, eightfold for a vaishya.
A brahmana should not eat elsewhere having been previously invited by a brahmin; a younger one in the killing of an animal would be equal in dharma.
If, however, being invited by a kshatriya or vaishya, he eats, the younger one in the killing of an animal would incur half the share.
A brahmana who eats at the rite for gods or ancestors without bathing, king, incurs the unrighteousness of a false statement about cows.
An impure brahmana, king, who eats at a brahmana's rite knowingly or from greed incurs the unrighteousness of a false statement about cows.
One who seeks grain by grain or for a work's sake, Bharata, and invites, king of kings, incurs unrighteousness, remembered as untruth.
Those who have not the Veda, vows or conduct, Yudhishthira, if served with mantras by the three classes, in them is the unrighteousness of a false statement about cows.
[Yudhishthira said:] I wish to hear to whom, grandfather, a gift for ancestors or gods is of great fruit.
[Bhishma said:] Feed those whose wives wait for them as farmers for good rain, Yudhishthira, with the remainder of what is left over.
Those bound by conduct, lean, of slender livelihood, who come asking, king: a gift to them has great fruit.
Those devoted to him, whose house and wealth and refuge are in him, and who come to him for his gift: a gift to them has great fruit.
Those afraid of thieves or others, Yudhishthira, who come asking to eat: a gift to them has great fruit.
A gift to those whose boys beg for the sinless brahmana who has made alms-gleaning his practice has great fruit.
A gift to brahmanas whose wealth and wives were taken in the ruin of a country, who come asking for a purpose, has great fruit.
A gift to brahmanas with vows, steady in rules, approved in the Veda, who wish to complete it, has great fruit.
A gift to those who have not transgressed dharma or the agreements of heresies, lean in life and wealth, has great fruit.
A gift to those who, stripped of all they own, though faultless, by the powerful, long for food that has been eaten has great fruit.
A gift to ascetics devoted to austerity and those who wander begging, who ask for something, has great fruit.
The rule of great fruit in giving has been heard by you, bull of the Bharatas; hear also by what men go to hell and heaven.
Except for the teacher's sake or for safety's, Yudhishthira, those who tell untruth go to hell.
Those who carry off another's wives, who touch another's wives, who send others to another's wives go to hell.
Those who steal another's property, who destroy others' goods, who inform on others go to hell.
Men who break down water-sheds, assembly halls, bridges and houses, Bharata, go to hell.
Men who cheat the helpless, a woman, a child, the old, the frightened or ascetics go to hell.
Those who cut off livelihood, home, wife, Bharata, a friend, or hope go to hell.
Informers, breakers of agreement, those who live on another's livelihood, and ingrates to friends go to hell.
Heretics, corrupters, and defilers of agreements, and those who return to them go to hell.
Those who by dividing take away a man's hope, his settlement, his food and his labour go to hell.
Those who eat before their wives, the fire-servants and guests, and those who neglect rites to ancestors and gods go to hell.
Sellers of the Veda, defilers of the Vedas, and writers of the Vedas go to hell.
Men outside the four stages and outside scripture, who live by bad deeds, go to hell.
Sellers of hair, king, sellers of poison, and sellers of milk go to hell.
Those who come between brahmanas, cows and maidens, Yudhishthira, in their affairs go to hell.
Sellers of weapons and makers of arrows and bows, Yudhishthira, go to hell.
Those who obstruct a road with arrows, stakes or pits, bull of the Bharatas, go to hell.
Those who abandon teachers, servants and devotees when they are unable, bull of the Bharatas, go to hell.
Those who tame animals not ready, who pierce noses, and who bind animals go to hell.
Those who do not protect, who deceive in goods, who are intent on the sixth share, and who are able but do not give go to hell.
Those who abandon the patient, self-controlled and wise, who have lived with them long, when their task is done, go to hell.
Men who eat first without giving to children, the old and servants go to hell.
These who go to hell have been seen and told by earlier sages; I shall tell of those who share in the world of heaven, bull of the Bharatas.
In all rites that begin with the gods, Bharata, transgression against a brahmana destroys sons and all animals.
By giving, austerity and truth, Yudhishthira, men who follow dharma go to heaven.
Those who by service and austerity take up learning, Bharata, and are indifferent to accepting gifts, go to heaven.
Those who are freed from fear, sin, hindrance, poverty and harassment by disease, by what is done for them, go to heaven.
The forgiving and steady, bent on acts of dharma and joined with auspicious conduct, go to heaven.
Those who have turned from honey and meat, from others' wives, and from intoxicating drink go to heaven.
Makers of hermitages, of families, Bharata, of countries and towns go to heaven.
Givers of garments and ornaments, givers of food and drink, and givers to families go to heaven.
Men who have turned from all violence, who bear everything, and who are the refuge of all go to heaven.
Those who serve mother and father, masters of their senses, and are affectionate to their brothers go to heaven.
The rich and strong, Bharata, established in youth, who are masters of their senses and steady, go to heaven.
Those who are affectionate to the offending, gentle, kind to friends and easy to please go to heaven.
Those who surround and feed a thousand, give a thousand, and save a thousand go to heaven.
Givers of gold, of cows, bull of the Bharatas, of carriages and vehicles go to heaven.
Givers of maidens in marriage, of servants, Yudhishthira, and of garments go to heaven.
Those who give pleasure-grounds, rest-houses, gardens, wells, groves, halls, and who build embankments go to heaven.
Givers of houses, fields and dwellings, Bharata, and of what is sought go to heaven.
Men who give juices, seeds and grains, Yudhishthira, having produced them themselves, go to heaven.
This has been said for the other world, the rite for gods and for ancestors, Bharata, and the dharma and adharma of giving as made by earlier sages.
[Bhishma said:] I shall tell you, king of kings, what I once asked Vyasa when I addressed him; listen to that with one mind.
You, the fourth after Vasishtha, tell me the truth, sage: without killing, by what is the killing of a brahmana ordained here?
Thus asked, great king, Parashara's son, skilled in dharma, said what is without doubt unsurpassed:

He who himself calls a lean-living brahmana for alms and afterward says 'There is none', know him a killer of a brahmana.
mahabharata:13:25.6	He who, evil-minded, takes the livelihood of a neutral learned brahmana, Bharata, know him a killer of a brahmana.
mahabharata:13:25.7	He who creates an obstacle for a herd of cows thirsty for water, lord of the earth, know him a killer of a brahmana.
mahabharata:13:25.8	He who, without understanding, disparages the scripture rightly set going or a treatise made by sages, know him a killer of a brahmana.
mahabharata:13:25.9	He who does not give his daughter, grown and endowed with beauty, to a suitable groom, know him a killer of a brahmana.
mahabharata:13:25.10	The fool devoted to unrighteousness who falsely gives the twice-born a grief that reaches the vitals, know him a killer of a brahmana.
mahabharata:13:25.11	He who takes all the property of a man blind of eye, or lame, or dull, know him a killer of a brahmana.
mahabharata:13:25.12	He who from delusion sets fire in a hermitage, forest, village or city, know him a killer of a brahmana.
[Yudhishthira said:] Of the holy sacred fords on earth, bull of the Bharatas, you ought to tell me; I shall listen restrained, lord.
[Bhishma said:] You ought to hear this lineage of sacred fords told by Angiras, greatly radiant one; good fortune to you, you will gain supreme dharma.
Going to the great sage, a brahmana in the penance-grove, the hero Gautama of sharp vows asked Angiras:

Blessed one, I have a doubt of dharma about sacred fords; I wish to hear it all; tell me, great sage.
mahabharata:13:26.6	What fruit is there, sage, from bathing in those fords, in the world after death? Tell me, greatly wise one, as it is.
[Angiras said:] "One who for seven days, fasting and free of mine-ness, plunges into the Vitasta, the river garlanded with waves, in Chandrabhaga, becomes like a sage.
The rivers in the Kashmir region that fall into the great river: a virtuous man gaining those rivers and the Sindhu would attain heaven.
Plunging into Pushkara, Prabhasa, Naimisha, the sea water, the Devika, the Indra road and Svarnabindu, he awakes standing in a celestial car, praised by apsarases.
Where the Ganga Bhagirathi goes toward the north, at the place of Maheshvara, the man who is consecrated there fasting for one month himself sees the gods.
Satisfying at Saptaganga, Triganga and Indramarga, a man gains nectar to enjoy and is not born again.
One who, pure and devoted to the Agnihotra, touches the water at Mahashrama, fasting one month, would go to success in a month.
Touching the water at Mahahrada on Bhrigutunga, ungreedy, having fasted three nights, he is freed from the killing of a brahmana.
Touching water at Kanyakupa and making water-offering at Balaka, he gains fame among the gods and shines with glory.
Touching water at Deshakala and the lake Sundarika, a man gains from the Ashvins beauty and splendour after death.
Touching the Mahaganga at Krittikangaraka, fasting a fortnight, he gains heaven, pure.
Touching water at Vaimanika and at Kinkinikashrama, he is honoured, going at will, in the divine dwelling of the apsarases.
Reaching the Kalikashrama and making water-offering at the Vipasha, a celibate with anger conquered is freed from rebirth in three nights.
He who bathes at the hermitage of the Krittikas and satisfies his ancestors, having pleased Mahadeva, would gain heaven, pure.
Touching water at Mahapura and fasting three nights, a man would be free of fear from moving and unmoving beings and two-footed ones.
Bathing in the Devadaru forest and making water-offering, his sins shaken off, pure, staying seven nights, he gains the world of the gods.
Bathing at Kaushanta, Kushastamba, Drona Sharmapada and at Apah Prapatana, he is attended by troops of apsarases.
Plunging into the waters of Chitrakuta, Janasthana and Mandakini, fasting, he gains royal fortune.
Going to the hermitage of Shyama and living and bathing there, he would stay three nights times three and live in the city of the gandharvas.
Touching water at Ramanya and at Gandhatarika, fasting a month, he would gain the fruit of invisibility.
Reaching the door of the Kaushiki, living on air, ungreedy, a man ascends to heaven in twenty-one nights.
One who bathes in the Matanga well succeeds in one night, and plunges into the Andhaka, supportless and eternal.
Touching water at Naimisha and at Svargatirtha, master of his senses, making water-offering for a month he would gain the fruit of a human sacrifice.
Touching water at the Ganga lake and in the Utpala forest, he gains the horse sacrifice, making water-offering there a month.
At the ford of the Ganga and Yamuna, on the mountain Kalanjara, touching the water at Shashtihrada, no other gift is more distinguished.
Ten thousand sacred fords and three ten million others come together at Prayaga in Magha, bull of the Bharatas.
Bathing at Prayaga in the month of Magha, restrained and of sharp vows, best of the Bharatas, he would attain heaven, pure.
Touching water at Marudgana in the hermitage of the ancestors, pure, and at the ford of Vaivasvata, a man becomes himself a sacred ford.
So going to Brahmashiras and making water-offering in the Bhagirathi, fasting one month, he would reach the world of Soma.
Bathing at Kapotaka and making water-offering at Ashtavakra, fasting twelve days, a man would gain the fruit of a human sacrifice.
At Munjaprishtha, Gaya, Nirriti, Devaparvata, and the third, Krauncapadi, he is purified from the killing of a brahmana.
Touching water at Kalashi and often at the Vedi, at Agnipura, bathing, and making water-offering at Vishala, touching the water at Devahrada, he shines as one who has become Brahman.
Serving Purapavartana, Nanda and Mahananda, one is attended in Nandana, self-controlled and harmless, by apsarases.
One who, well-composed, goes at the conjunction of Urvashi and the Krittikas, bathing duly in the Lauhitya, would gain the fruit of a lotus.
Touching water at Ramahrada and making water-offering at Vishala, fasting twelve days, he is freed from stain.
Touching water at Mahahrada with a pure mind, a man fasting one month would gain the goal of Jamadagni.
Heating himself on the Vindhya, true to his word and harmless, taking a stand six months, he is purified in one month.
Touching water in the Narmada and at the water of Surparaka, fasting a fortnight, he is made a king's son.
On the Jambu road, restrained and well-composed for three months, in one day and night he attains success.
Plunging into the waters at Kokamukha and going to the hermitage of Chandalika, eating vegetables and wearing bark, he wins ten maidens.
He would never go to Vaivasvata's house; one who stays at Kanyahrada goes to the world of the gods.
At Prabhasa, composed for one night at the new moon, mighty-armed, he succeeds, the man who is not born again.
Touching water at Ujjanaka and at the hermitage of Arshtishena, bathing at the hermitage of Pingaya, he is freed from all sins.
Touching water at Kulya and muttering the Aghamarshana, fasted three nights, pure, he gains the horse sacrifice.
Touching water at Pindaraka and staying one night, a man, pure through the night to morning, gains the Agnishtoma.
So going to Brahmasara, adorned with Dharmaranya, pure through the night to morning, he gains the lotus.
Bathing on the Mainaka mountain and worshipping at twilight, having conquered desire for a month, he gains the fruit of the all-sacrifice.
The famous holy Himalaya, Shankara's father-in-law, a mine of all jewels, served by Siddhas and Charanas,
there one may give up the body by rule, by fasting, a twice-born who has crossed the Vedanta, knowing life to be impermanent.
Having worshipped the gods there and saluted the sages, then a perfected one goes to heaven, the eternal world of Brahma.
One who dwells at a sacred ford having conquered desire, anger and greed has not failed to gain anything by going to a ford.
The fords that are inaccessible, hard and rough should be gone to by mind, in summary of all fords.
This is pure, blessed, leading to heaven, happy; this is the secret of the gods, a purifier of those who bathe.
One should give this to the twice-born, to good men, to one's son, or mutter it in the ear of a friend or a loyal pupil.
The great ascetic Angiras gave this to Gautama, permitted by teachers and by the wise Kashyapa.
This is the best prayer of great sages that purify; muttering it and rising constantly, he would reach heaven, pure.
One who hears this secret, held by Angiras, gains birth in an excellent family and remembers his birth.
Ganga's son, of great splendour, was struck down by Arjuna in battle; Yudhishthira attended him with his brothers and others.
To see the unfallen best of the Bharatas lying on his hero's bed awaiting time, great sages came.
Atri, Vasishtha, Bhrigu, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Angiras, Gautama, Agastya, Sumati, Svayu, Atmavat,
Vishvamitra, Sthulashiras, Samvarta, Pramati, Dama, Ushanas, Brihaspati, Vyasa, Chyavana, Kashyapa, Dhruva,
Durvasas, Jamadagni, Markandeya, Galava, Bharadvaja, Raibhya, Yavakrita, Trita,
Sthulaksha, Shakalaksha, Kanva, Medhatithi, Krisha, Narada, Parvata, Sudhanva, Ekata and Dvita,
Nitambhu, Bhuvana, Dhaumya, Shatananda, Akritavrana, Rama Jamadagnya, Kamya and the others: the great sages came to see Bhishma.
Yudhishthira with his brothers duly honoured those great souls who had come, in order.
Hearing the talk of those sages of purified selves, Bhishma thought himself in heaven, joined with supreme contentment.
Then those great sages, taking leave of Bhishma and the Pandavas, all vanished as everyone watched.
Even after those greatly fortunate sages had vanished, all the Pandavas praised them and bowed again and again.
With pleased minds, all the best of the Kurus attended Ganga's son as knowers of mantra attend the rising sun.
Seeing the power of austerity of those sages, the Pandavas, seeing all directions shining, came to the highest wonder.
Reflecting on the great fortune of those sages, the Pandavas held talks with Bhishma on that subject.
At the end of the talk, touching Bhishma's feet with his head, the Pandava Yudhishthira, son of Dharma, asked a question of dharma:
Which lands, which countries, which hermitages and which mountains are the best in merit, and which rivers are to be known, grandfather?
[Bhishma said:] On this too they recite this ancient Itihasa, a conversation of a gleaner of grain and a perfected one, Yudhishthira.
A certain one, best of men, having circled this earth adorned with mountains many times, came to the house of the best of householders, a gleaner.
Honoured by him by rule, the fulfilled one waited upon that perfected guest.
The two great souls, seated at ease, held auspicious talks joined to the Veda, marked by the remnant of it.
At the end of the talk the wise gleaner took leave of the perfected one with effort and asked the question which you ask me.
[The gleaner said:] "Which lands, which countries, which hermitages and which mountains are best in merit, and which rivers are to be known? Let that be said."
[The perfected one said:] "Those lands, those countries, those hermitages and those mountains are best through the middle of which the Ganga Bhagirathi, best of rivers, flows.
By austerity, celibacy, sacrifice or renunciation a creature would not gain that goal which one gains serving the Ganga.
For those whose bodies were touched by waters of the Ganga, once placed, there is no again abandoning heaven.
Those embodied beings for whom all rites were done with Ganga's waters, Brahmana, leaving the cow, stay in heaven immovable.
Even men who did sinful deeds in earlier life and afterward serve the Ganga go to the highest goal.
The blessing that comes to men who bathe in the pure waters of the Ganga with controlled mind is not got even by hundreds of sacrifices.
As long as a man's bone stays in the waters of the Ganga, so many thousand years he is honoured, having reached heaven.
Thus addressed by the great sage Narada, Marutta told him all that had been deceived by his priest.
But if I am to be favoured and am dear to you, let food be made first, and then we shall learn.
Then Arjuna, dear friend of Keshava, took leave of them and set out to see his maternal uncle, saying, "This is not so."
In another part the descendant of the Kurus saw Karna, best of weapon-bearers, accompanied by the twelve Adityas.
